title: Dispatch BBA 2: New Dates Appear in Old Hospital Register
summary: The names belong to patients who died more than fifty years ago.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: Archivist Agnes Morrow yesterday showed this newspaper six new entries in the surviving admission register of St. Oran's Fever Hospital. The entries are dated June 1874 and name patients whose deaths were recorded in the same month.

The register has been kept in a locked municipal cabinet for twenty years. Miss Morrow found the writing identical to the original entries in ink, pressure, and letter formation. The paper shows no sign of tampering or recent handling.

Among the names is Sister Beatrice Kells, a nurse who stayed to open the east ward while patients were evacuated. Her death was recorded on the night of the fire. The new entry places her admission on the morning of the same day.

The Institute examined the new dates in ordinary light and through an Eidetic comparison lens. Through the lens, the entries appeared to emit a faint sonance consistent with the hospital fire. Dr. Saye described the effect as "a record that has not finished recording."

The bell rang once while the register was open. Miss Morrow saw an additional stroke of ink form at the bottom of the page before the sound ended. The new line contained her own name and today's date.
